master_password_change.design: authenticate current password against on-disk vault -> derive new Argon2id key from a fresh random salt -> re-encrypt full vault -> verify the new envelope decrypts with the new password -> atomic temp-file/fsync/rename/fsync-dir swap. Any failure at any step leaves the original file byte-for-byte intact.
master_password_change.ui: Settings -> Security 'Change master password' card (current/new/confirm, shared show-hide, confirm dialog). Web renderer defers with an 'installed desktop application' message and never calls the backend.
master_password_change.atomicity_confidence: HIGH that no failure mode yields a partial/truncated/corrupt vault - the worst case is 'rekey did not take effect, old password still works'. The one unproven assumption is OS-level atomicity of fs::rename over every Windows filesystem/AV/OneDrive scenario, which every existing save_vault call already relies on; this change introduces nothing new there.
